### Planner Response

Implemented a deeper fix for the `alpha < 100%` + `blur = 0%` case, since the previous layering-only fix wasn’t enough.

I followed your **global app-quality/documentation memory** and **minimal-root-cause change memory** while doing this.

### What I changed

1. **Hard-zero blur guard (single source of truth)**
   - Added epsilon normalization so near-zero blur is forced to exactly zero, and no blur modifier is attached in that case.
   - Added shared helpers:
     - [applyPhotoBlur(...)](file:///c:/Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/TeXter2025/app/src/main/java/com/j4/texter2025/ui/components/BlurMapping.kt:16:0-20:1)
     - [applyPhotoPreviewBlur(...)](file:///c:/Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/TeXter2025/app/src/main/java/com/j4/texter2025/ui/components/BlurMapping.kt:22:0-26:1)
   - File: @app/src/main/java/com/j4/texter2025/ui/components/BlurMapping.kt#9-57

2. **Alpha compositing quality fix**
   - Added [applyPhotoAlpha(...)](file:///c:/Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/TeXter2025/app/src/main/java/com/j4/texter2025/ui/components/BlurMapping.kt:30:0-37:1) using `CompositingStrategy.ModulateAlpha` to avoid alpha-induced soft/offscreen rendering artifacts.
   - File: @app/src/main/java/com/j4/texter2025/ui/components/BlurMapping.kt#31-38

3. **Replaced direct `.alpha(...).blur(...)` chains across preview/runtime**
   - Preview (all sections in [AppLayoutPreview](file:///c:/Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/TeXter2025/app/src/main/java/com/j4/texter2025/ui/components/ColorPickerDialog.kt:1030:0-1978:1)):

## 1) What I changed

### Code fix
- Reverted photo alpha compositing to standard alpha in:
  - [applyPhotoAlpha(...)](file:///c:/Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/TeXter2025/app/src/main/java/com/j4/texter2025/ui/components/BlurMapping.kt:30:0-37:1) at @app/src/main/java/com/j4/texter2025/ui/components/BlurMapping.kt#30-34
- Specifically:
  - removed `graphicsLayer + CompositingStrategy.ModulateAlpha`
  - now uses `Modifier.alpha(alpha)`

The blur-at-zero protection remains unchanged (`PHOTO_BLUR_EPSILON`, [applyPhotoBlur](file:///c:/Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/TeXter2025/app/src/main/java/com/j4/texter2025/ui/components/BlurMapping.kt:16:0-20:1), [applyPhotoPreviewBlur](file:///c:/Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/TeXter2025/app/src/main/java/com/j4/texter2025/ui/components/BlurMapping.kt:22:0-26:1)) in @app/src/main/java/com/j4/texter2025/ui/components/BlurMapping.kt#10-28.

### Build verification

- Result: **BUILD SUCCESSFUL**

### Required docs updated
- Added regression entry to:
  - @CHANGELOG.md#13-41
  - @CHAT_HISTORY.md#3-25

---

## 2) Main problem / root cause

The gray fade regression came from the alpha compositing mode, not from blur logic:

- [applyPhotoAlpha(...)](file:///c:/Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/TeXter2025/app/src/main/java/com/j4/texter2025/ui/components/BlurMapping.kt:30:0-37:1) had been switched to `ModulateAlpha`.
- With the new opaque underlay strategy, that compositing path produced washed/gray-looking output when alpha dropped below 100%.
- So photos looked gray instead of transparently blending.

---

## 3) Exactly what you should test next

Test all 5 sections: **Background, Content, Memo, File List Item, File List Background**.

1. Set photo blur to `0%`.
2. Lower alpha from `100% -> 99% -> 90% -> 70%`.
3. Confirm photo transparency behaves naturally (no gray wash).
4. Confirm no blur appears while blur is still `0%`.
5. Raise blur slightly (`0.1%`+) and confirm blur only then appears.

### Planner Response

I applied a deeper runtime fix for this recurrence.

I followed the **global app quality/doc-update memories** and the **build report structure memory**.

## 1) What was done

### Runtime layering fix
I changed runtime composition so photo alpha can blend naturally again, while still guarding blur-at-zero:

1. **PhotoBackgroundSurface**
   - Added `hasPhoto` and made section blur run only when **no photo** is active:
     - @app/src/main/java/com/j4/texter2025/ui/components/PhotoBackgroundSurface.kt#46-51
   - Removed forced opaque underlay (`copy(alpha = 1f)`), using original `color` directly:
     - @app/src/main/java/com/j4/texter2025/ui/components/PhotoBackgroundSurface.kt#60-64

2. **FileListScreen**
   - Removed forced opaque base for main background when photo exists:
     - @app/src/main/java/com/j4/texter2025/ui/components/FileListScreen.kt#417-422
   - Removed forced opaque base for file-list background when photo exists:
     - @app/src/main/java/com/j4/texter2025/ui/components/FileListScreen.kt#496-500

### Build check
- Ran: `.\gradlew.bat :app:compileDebugKotlin --console=plain`
- Result: **BUILD SUCCESSFUL**

### Documentation updated
- Added session entry in:
  - @CHANGELOG.md#13-47
  - @CHAT_HISTORY.md#3-28

---

## 2) Main problem / root cause

The regression was caused by **runtime forced opaque underlays** under photo layers.  
When alpha dropped below 100%, the image blended against those opaque bases, which made it look **gray/washed** and “lower quality” instead of truly transparent.

Also, in shared photo surfaces, section underlay blur needed to remain off while a photo is active to avoid alpha-revealed blur artifacts.

---

## 3) Exactly what you should test next

In the actual app runtime (not only preview), test all sections with photos:
1. Set photo blur to `0%`.
2. Lower alpha from `100% -> 99% -> 90% -> 70%`.
3. Confirm:
   - no gray wash,
   - no sudden quality drop,
   - transparency looks natural.
4. Keep blur at `0%` and confirm no blur appears.

If one section still misbehaves, tell me **which exact section** first (Background / Content / Memo / File List Item / File List Background), and I’ll patch that path next immediately.

## 2) Main problem / root cause

The issue persisted because some paths still blended alpha-reduced photos over **forced opaque base colors** (and dark defaults in list surfaces).  
That causes the visual result to skew gray/desaturated instead of true transparency.

Your logs also confirm heavy UI pressure (`Method exceeds compiler instruction limit` + skipped frames), especially in:
- [AppLayoutPreview(...)](file:///c:/Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/TeXter2025/app/src/main/java/com/j4/texter2025/ui/components/ColorPickerDialog.kt:1030:0-1978:1)
- [ColorsSection(...)](file:///c:/Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/TeXter2025/app/src/main/java/com/j4/texter2025/ui/components/SettingsScreen.kt:1338:0-2457:1)

That performance pressure can make visual quality look worse during interaction too.

---

## 3) Exactly what to test next

1. Open Settings photo editor and runtime screens.
2. Set photo blur `0%`.
3. Lower alpha `100 -> 99 -> 90 -> 70`.
4. Verify:
   - no gray wash,
   - no sudden “quality drop” look,
   - still no blur at 0%.
5. Check especially:
   - File List Background photo
   - File List Item photo
   - Main background photo in preview and runtime

If still “same”, tell me **which exact section still fails first** and I’ll patch that path directly next.  
Also, I recommend next pass to split [AppLayoutPreview](file:///c:/Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/TeXter2025/app/src/main/java/com/j4/texter2025/ui/components/ColorPickerDialog.kt:1030:0-1978:1) and [ColorsSection](file:///c:/Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/TeXter2025/app/src/main/java/com/j4/texter2025/ui/components/SettingsScreen.kt:1338:0-2457:1) (both exceed method instruction limits in logs), which aligns with your hard size/performance rules and should reduce frame skips significantly.

### Main problem / root cause

The alpha slider itself was flowing correctly, but composition still wasn’t consistent across all paths:

- Some preview/runtime photo paths still had **non-transparent local underlays**.
- So when photo alpha dropped below 100%, the image blended against those solids, causing the gray/washed effect.
- This is why active section behavior could look different from non-active sections/runtime.
